logic_node.action_detail: Patients with HF should receive care from multidisciplinary teams to facilitate the implementation of GDMT, address potential barriers to self-care, reduce the risk of subsequent rehospitalization for HF, and improve survival.

source_text: Patients with HF should receive care from multidisciplinary teams to facilitate the implementation of GDMT, address potential barriers to self-care, reduce the risk of subsequent rehospitalization for HF, and improve survival.

logic_node.action: Provide HF self-care education and support
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with HF should receive specific education and support to facilitate HF self-care in a multidisciplinary manner, including medication adherence, sodium restriction, physical activity, and symptom monitoring.

source_text: Patients with HF should receive specific education and support to facilitate HF self-care in a multidisciplinary manner.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, vaccinating against respiratory illnesses (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19) is reasonable to reduce mortality. Influenza vaccination was associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality.

source_text: In patients with HF, vaccinating against respiratory illnesses is reasonable to reduce mortality.

logic_node.action: Screen for depression, social isolation, frailty, and low health literacy
logic_node.action_detail: In adults with HF, screening for depression, social isolation, frailty, and low health literacy as risk factors for poor self-care is reasonable to improve management. Tools include PHQ-9 for depression, Fried frailty phenotype for frailty, SAHL/REALM-SF for health literacy.

source_text: In adults with HF, screening for depression, social isolation, frailty, and low health literacy as risk factors for poor self-care is reasonable to improve management.

logic_node.action_detail: For patients with stage C HF, avoiding excessive sodium intake is reasonable to reduce congestive symptoms. AHA recommends reduction of sodium intake to less than 2300 mg/d for general cardiovascular health, though no trials support this specific threshold in HF. Aggressive sodium restriction (0.8 g/d) has not shown benefit.

source_text: For patients with stage C HF, avoiding excessive sodium intake is reasonable to reduce congestive symptoms.

logic_node.action: Recommend exercise training or regular physical activity
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with HF who are able to participate, exercise training (or regular physical activity) is recommended to improve functional status, exercise performance, and quality of life. Benefits include improved endothelial function, blunted catecholamine spillover, increased peripheral oxygen extraction, and improvement in peak oxygen consumption.

source_text: For patients with HF who are able to participate, exercise training (or regular physical activity) is recommended to improve functional status, exercise performance, and QOL.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, a cardiac rehabilitation program can be useful to improve functional capacity, exercise tolerance, and health-related quality of life. Program includes medical evaluation, education regarding medical adherence, dietary recommendations, psychosocial support, and exercise training.

source_text: In patients with HF, a cardiac rehabilitation program can be useful to improve functional capacity, exercise tolerance, and health-related QOL.
